facts.text: The environment class SimpleDroneEnv subclasses gym.Env
The action space is a Box of four float32 values in [0, 1]
The observation space is a Box of shape (3, 3) whose low and high are both -inf
The environment constructs Drone(0, 0, 2, enable_death=False) and sets init_position to [0, 0, 2]
The environment stores the module constant NULL_ROT and step multiplies the action by it before Drone.step
NULL_ROT = 620.2943
Drone.step maps four values to w1 = v0, w2 = -v1, w3 = v2, w4 = -v3 and then calls update
The observation has three rows: [x, y, z], [ax, ay, az] and [p, q, r]
The reward is 1 - dist(current, init_position) / dist(goal_position, init_position)
A roll or pitch beyond 60 degrees or a z below 0 sets done, resets the drone and subtracts 5 from the reward; a distance below 0.01 from init_position sets done and adds 10
Step returns (observation, reward, done, info), the legacy four-value API
Reset takes no seed and no options; it calls Drone.__reset__ and returns the observation
Drone.__reset__ restores the position (0, 0, 0.5) and zeroes the angles, velocities and p, q, r
The simulation advances by a fixed step DT = 0.004 between updates
The drone parameters are mass 0.468, K = 2.980e-6, B = 1.140e-7, L = 0.225 and G = 9.8
The inertia is IXX = IYY = 4.856e-3 and IZZ = 8.801e-3
The drag coefficients are AX = AY = AZ = 0.25
Thrust is K times the sum of the four squared rotor speeds along body z
Acceleration is gravity plus (1/mass) times the rotated thrust plus (1/mass) times the drag force
p, q and r are overwritten with the angular acceleration from the inertia and the torque
update integrates with Euler steps: angle += angular velocity*DT, velocity += acceleration*DT and position += the updated velocity*DT
normalise_theta keeps an angle in the -pi to pi range

determinism.notes: the rigid-body update is deterministic and the upstream reset() restores a fixed state without using the seed; the bridge records the seed, so one seed and a command sequence repeat, but different seeds do not change the trajectory

gaps: rigid-body dynamics with an ideal rotor-to-thrust and rotor-to-torque mapping: no contact model, no ground or obstacle collision; a z below 0 or a tilt beyond 60 degrees simply resets the drone
the rotor speed is an ideal input (action * NULL_ROT); there is no motor, battery, aerodynamic or sensor-noise model in the environment
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by 4 ms only
the fake backend re-implements the dynamics in pure Python with nested lists rather than numpy float32 arrays, and it was not compared with a run of the upstream environment
seed control is nominal: the upstream reset() takes no seed and restores the same fixed state, so the seed is recorded but does not change the trajectory
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the fake does not render; upstream render() calls a matplotlib Graphics window

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
